title: CEO Interview with Andrew Seddon of CircuitHub
gist: CircuitHub CEO Andrew Seddon says its automated high-mix PCB assembly system 'The Grid' in Massachusetts has reached price parity with comparable Chinese manufacturers at a 4-day average turnaround versus 9 for a typical Chinese quick-turn shop. The company has shipped 2.2M+ boards to 26,000+ engineers, is expanding Massachusetts capacity fivefold and plans a UK factory in 2027.

insights.claim: CircuitHub says it has reached price parity with comparable manufacturers in China, with an average turnaround of four days versus nine for a typical Chinese quick-turn shop.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Automation may erode China's cost advantage in low-volume PCB assembly, supporting reshoring.
insights.quote: We have now reached price parity with comparable manufacturers in China, with an average turnaround of four days versus nine for a typical Chinese quick-turn shop.

insights.claim: CircuitHub's architecture of per-board routing makes small-batch electronics production competitive onshore in the US.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Supports a US reshoring narrative for prototype and low-volume electronics.

insights.claim: CircuitHub is increasing capacity at its Massachusetts site fivefold and plans to open a UK factory in 2027.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Capacity expansion signals strong demand for fast-turn onshore assembly.
insights.quote: We are increasing capacity at our Massachusetts site fivefold and plan to open a UK factory in 2027.

insights.claim: CircuitHub has shipped more than 2.2 million boards, placed over 150 million components and served more than 26,000 engineers.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Scale metrics for an automated EMS challenger.

insights.claim: Around 95% of electronics projects involve fewer than 10,000 units, leaving many teams underserved by manufacturers geared to mass production.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Defines a large, underserved low-volume market segment.
insights.quote: Around 95% of projects involve fewer than 10,000 units

insights.claim: High-volume electronics manufacturing is highly automated, but small-batch, high-mix production still depends heavily on people operating machines and coordinating production.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Automation opportunity lies in high-mix, not high-volume, assembly.

insights.claim: CircuitHub's The Grid uses levitating movers to carry boards between robots for solder paste printing, placement, soldering and inspection, with software and AI routing each board individually so 1 unit of 100 designs runs as easily as 100 units of one design.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Fab-inspired automation applied to PCB assembly removes changeover costs.
insights.quote: One unit of 100 designs can run as easily as 100 units of one design.

insights.claim: CircuitHub takes inspiration from semiconductor fabs, applying techniques from highly automated chip manufacturing to electronics assembly.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Cross-pollination of fab automation into downstream electronics assembly.

insights.claim: CircuitHub's R&D is predominantly software, using classical control and computer vision, and it is exploring AI agents for higher-level factory control.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Agentic AI is beginning to reach factory control.

themes.theme: AI raises value of fast iteration

insights.claim: As AI accelerates hardware design, the ability to manufacture quickly becomes increasingly important because teams need to build and test what they design.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Physical prototyping speed may become the bottleneck as AI speeds up design.
insights.quote: As AI accelerates design, the ability to manufacture quickly becomes increasingly important.

insights.claim: CircuitHub's customers include a leading US electric vehicle manufacturer and one of the world's largest AI labs, plus engineers in self-driving vehicles, satellites, robotics and industrial equipment.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Demand for fast-turn hardware is coming from AI, EV and space sectors.
